detail.body:
## What

Adds the `world_size` axis to CI, which the current suite does not cover:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/cpu-torch-multi-latest.yml` | Nightly + manual dispatch: runs the multi-rank CPU tests on a 4-vCPU runner |
| `.github/workflows/cpu-multi-triage.yml` | Routes its outcome through the existing `ci/nightly_classify.sh` / `ci/nightly_report.sh` protocol |
| `tests/conftest.py` | The `DS_MULTIRANK_ONLY` collection hook the workflow selects with (required) |
| `.github/workflows/TEST_SELECTION.md` | Registration of the new nightly |

## Why

`cpu-torch-latest` advertises a single device, so the per-device gate in
`tests/unit/common.py` skips **every `world_size > 1` test** on that runner. The
multi-rank path is therefore only exercised on GPU machines, and issues that show up
there only in a multi-rank configuration go unnoticed.

A recent example: PR #8638 changed the overflow semantics so that non-finite
group norms force an optimizer step to be skipped, bypassing
`bf16.check_grad_overflow: False`. `TestZeROBFloat16::test_ignore_grad_overflow` is
`world_size = 2`, so it is collected and *skipped* by the CPU CI and by any run with
one device; it fails as soon as two ranks execute. Reported as issue #8805.

## Why a nightly rather than a pre-merge check

The selection is cheap to state and expensive to run (measured in #8381, 4-vCPU
runner):

| Run | Wall time |
|---|---|
| This suite: non-v1 multi-rank half | 68-89 min |
| This suite: `sequential`-marked phase | 13-16 min |
| Longest current pre-merge job (`cpu-torch-latest`) | 39-43 min |
| Longest merge-queue job (`modal-torch-latest`) | 64-71 min |

Putting it in the pre-merge path would roughly triple the critical path of every PR,
and a single wedged rank would block the merge queue (the suite's known hang — the
shm op segfaulting on hosts without AVX512 — is fixed by #8701, but the suite is the
most expensive one to re-run).

## What it runs

- `LOCAL_SIZE=4` so the gate admits `world_size <= 4`; `DS_MULTIRANK_ONLY=1` deselects
  the single-rank tests that `cpu-torch-latest` already guards.
- Non-v1 half, `timeout 120m`, plus a `sequential`-marked phase, `timeout 25m` (the
  parallel phase deselects those by default, so they would otherwise never run here).
- Same preset/install/HF-predownload steps as `cpu-torch-latest`, so both runs agree on
  the environment.
- On failure the last step prints `DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS=timeout|test` for triage; a run
  that dies before that step is reported as unclassified rather than guessed.

Triage is a separate workflow with its own issue titles and its own
`nightly-cpu-multi-last-green` tag, so `nightly-last-green` keeps meaning "the last
revision the full GPU suite verified" and the modal issue dedupe is untouched.

## Validation

- Workflow YAML parses; `pre-commit` clean.
- Timings above come from the real runs of this configuration in #8381.
- Not yet run as `cpu-torch-multi-latest`: GitHub only exposes `workflow_dispatch` for
  workflows present on the default branch, so the first manual dispatch has to happen
  after this merges. Happy to run it then and follow up with the numbers.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+name: cpu-multi-triage
+
+# Regression triage for the nightly cpu-torch-multi-latest multi-rank run.
+#
+# It mirrors nightly-triage.yml (same DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS sentinel protocol and the
+# same deduplicating reporter) but keeps its own issue titles and its own
+# last-green tag, so the modal full-suite tag stays meaningful and the two nightlies
+# never comment on each other's issues:
+#   green  -> move the nightly-cpu-multi-last-green tag to the tested SHA
+#   infra  -> do nothing (capacity problem, no candidate information)
+#   timeout-> open an issue (a phase outgrew its `timeout` budget)
+#   unknown-> open an issue (no sentinel: the run died before the classifier ran)
+#   test   -> open an issue listing the failing tests
+#
+# Only scheduled runs on master are triaged; workflow_dispatch runs are for manual
+# debugging. Scripts are checked out at the SHA the nightly actually ran, so the
+# classifier and the sentinel protocol it parses come from the same revision.
+
+on:
+  workflow_run:
+    workflows: [cpu-torch-multi-latest]
+    types: [completed]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  triage:
+    if: >-
+      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'schedule' &&
+      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'master'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      actions: read
+    outputs:
+      action: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.action }}
+      failure_class: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.failure_class }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout triage scripts at the nightly SHA
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 1
+          persist-credentials: false
+          lfs: false
+          submodules: false
+
+      - name: Classify nightly outcome
+        id: classify
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          NIGHTLY_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+          NIGHTLY_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
+        run: bash ci/nightly_classify.sh
+
+  tag-green:
+    name: move nightly-cpu-multi-last-green tag
+    needs: triage
+    if: needs.triage.outputs.action == 'green'
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      # The nightly SHA, not master: master advances during the run and the tag must
+      # point at the revision the suite actually verified.
+      - name: Checkout the nightly SHA
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 1
+
+      - name: Move the nightly-cpu-multi-last-green tag
+        env:
+          NIGHTLY_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+        run: |
+          git tag -f nightly-cpu-multi-last-green "$NIGHTLY_SHA"
+          git push -f origin nightly-cpu-multi-last-green
+
+  report-timeout:
+    name: report multi-rank timeout
+    needs: triage
+    if: needs.triage.outputs.action == 'timeout'
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      issues: write
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout report scripts at the nightly SHA
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+          lfs: false
+          submodules: false
+
+      - name: Report the timeout
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          NIGHTLY_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
+          NIGHTLY_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          FAILURE_CLASS: ${{ needs.triage.outputs.failure_class }}
+        # Title is deliberately SHA-free: a persistent timeout is one recurring issue
+        # that collects a comment per night, not one issue per night.
+        run: |
+          {
+            echo "The nightly multi-rank CPU run died at its time budget (class: $FAILURE_CLASS) at $NIGHTLY_SHA."
+            echo "The multi-rank suite likely outgrew its 120m/25m phase budgets; consider raising them or splitting the suite. Run: $NIGHTLY_RUN_URL"
+          } > issue-body.txt
+          bash ci/nightly_report.sh \
+            "nightly timeout: cpu-torch-multi-latest multi-rank suite exceeded its time budget" \
+            issue-body.txt "$NIGHTLY_RUN_URL"
+
+  report-unknown:
+    name: report unclassified multi-rank failure
+    needs: triage
+    if: needs.triage.outputs.action == 'unknown'
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      issues: write
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout report scripts at the nightly SHA
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+          lfs: false
+          submodules: false
+
+      - name: Report the unclassified failure
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          NIGHTLY_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
+          NIGHTLY_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+        # No sentinel means the run died before the classifier step (checkout, venv,
+        # dependency install, or a job kill). That is a different situation from a
+        # phase timeout and gets its own issue.
+        run: |
+          {
+            echo "The nightly multi-rank CPU run at $NIGHTLY_SHA failed without a DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS sentinel."
+            echo "The run died before the classifier step (checkout, venv, or dependency install). Triage manually."
+            echo "Run: $NIGHTLY_RUN_URL"
+          } > issue-body.txt
+          bash ci/nightly_report.sh \
+            "nightly failure without a failure class: cpu-torch-multi-latest died unclassified" \
+            issue-body.txt "$NIGHTLY_RUN_URL"
+
+  report-failures:
+    name: report multi-rank test failures
+    needs: triage
+    if: needs.triage.outputs.action == 'report'
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      actions: read
+      issues: write
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout report scripts at the nightly SHA
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+          lfs: false
+          submodules: false
+
+      - name: Extract the failing test files
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          NIGHTLY_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+        run: |
+          # The nightly pytest prints failures as "FAILED unit/..." (its working
+          # directory is tests/), so re-prefix each unique file with tests/.
+          gh run view "$NIGHTLY_RUN_ID" --log \
+            | grep -oE 'FAILED unit/[^[:space:]]*\.py' | sort -u \
+            | sed 's|^FAILED |tests/|' > failing-tests.txt
+          if [ ! -s failing-tests.txt ]; then
+            echo "no FAILED test files found in the nightly log" >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          cat failing-tests.txt
+
+      - name: Report the failures
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          NIGHTLY_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
+          NIGHTLY_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+        # Title is deliberately SHA-free (see report-timeout): the same regression
+        # recurring night after night is one tracked issue that collects a comment per
+        # occurrence, not a new issue per night.
+        run: |
+          {
+            echo "The nightly multi-rank CPU run at $NIGHTLY_SHA failed with real test failures."
+            echo "Failing test files:"
+            sed 's|^|- |' failing-tests.txt
+            echo
+            echo "Run: $NIGHTLY_RUN_URL"
+          } > issue-body.txt
+          bash ci/nightly_report.sh \
+            "nightly regression: cpu-torch-multi-latest multi-rank suite failed" \
+            issue-body.txt "$NIGHTLY_RUN_URL"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+name: cpu-torch-multi-latest
+
+# Multi-rank CPU suite.
+#
+# The plain cpu-torch-latest run advertises a single device, so the per-device gate in
+# tests/unit/common.py skips every world_size > 1 test there. This run sets LOCAL_SIZE
+# to let those tests execute and DS_MULTIRANK_ONLY to select only them, which keeps the
+# suite inside one job. It is what caught, among others, the bf16 overflow semantics
+# change from #8638 (reported as issue #8805).
+#
+# Nightly rather than a pull-request check: the suite needs roughly 1.5 h on a 4-vCPU
+# runner, and a wedged rank would hold up the merge queue. Regressions are reported
+# through cpu-multi-triage.yml, which parses the DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS sentinel this
+# workflow prints when it fails.
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      torch_preset:
+        description: PyTorch CPU preset to install for manual runs
+        required: false
+        default: '2.14.0-cpu'
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - '2.10.0-cpu'
+          - '2.14.0-cpu'
+      # Used only when a manual workflow_dispatch explicitly selects
+      # transformers_source=pypi. Scheduled nightlies and default manual runs
+      # install Transformers from Git and ignore this value.
+      transformers_version:
+        description: Hugging Face Transformers PyPI package version to install
+        required: false
+        default: '4.51.3'
+        type: string
+      transformers_source:
+        description: Hugging Face Transformers source for manual runs
+        required: false
+        default: 'git'
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - 'pypi'
+          - 'git'
+      transformers_ref:
+        description: Hugging Face Transformers git ref to install when source is git
+        required: false
+        default: 'main'
+        type: string
+  schedule:
+    # Off the 00:00 cluster (cpu-torch-latest, formatting, amd-mi200, hpu) and away
+    # from modal-torch-latest at 10:00, so the two CPU suites never share a runner pool.
+    - cron: "0 4 * * *"
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  unit-tests:
+    name: cpu-torch-multi-latest / unit tests
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Environment setup (~10m) + the two phases below with their own timeouts.
+    timeout-minutes: 200
+
+    env:
+      # CPU ranks are plain processes over gloo. Advertise 4 local devices so the
+      # per-device gate admits world_size <= 4 tests; the harness re-sets LOCAL_SIZE
+      # per worker, so this value only affects that gate.
+      LOCAL_SIZE: '4'
+      # Multi-rank tests churn mp pools; reused pools eventually hang in cleanup and
+      # stall workers. Fresh pools per test are slower but let the suite finish
+      # (knob documented in tests/unit/common.py).
+      DS_DISABLE_REUSE_DIST_ENV: '1'
+      # Run only the multi-rank tests this LOCAL_SIZE gate admits; the plain
+      # cpu-torch-latest run already guards the single-rank ones.
+      DS_MULTIRANK_ONLY: '1'
+      DEFAULT_TORCH_PRESET: '2.14.0-cpu'
+      DEFAULT_TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE: 'git'
+      # Manual PyPI fallback only; scheduled and default manual runs use Git.
+      DEFAULT_TRANSFORMERS_VERSION: '4.51.3'
+      DEFAULT_TRANSFORMERS_REF: 'main'
+
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+
+      - id: setup-venv
+        uses: ./.github/workflows/setup-venv
+
+      - name: Install system packages
+        run: |
+          sudo apt-get install -y numactl pdsh
+
+      - name: Resolve dependency inputs
+        env:
+          GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          MANUAL_TORCH_PRESET: ${{ github.event.inputs.torch_preset || '' }}
+          MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE: ${{ github.event.inputs.transformers_source || '' }}
+          MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.transformers_version || '' }}
+          MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_REF: ${{ github.event.inputs.transformers_ref || '' }}
+        run: |
+          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = 'workflow_dispatch' ] && [ -n "$MANUAL_TORCH_PRESET" ]; then
+            selected_preset="$MANUAL_TORCH_PRESET"
+          else
+            selected_preset="$DEFAULT_TORCH_PRESET"
+          fi
+
+          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = 'workflow_dispatch' ] && [ -n "$MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE" ]; then
+            transformers_source="$MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE"
+          else
+            transformers_source="$DEFAULT_TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE"
+          fi
+
+          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = 'workflow_dispatch' ] && [ -n "$MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_VERSION" ]; then
+            transformers_version="$MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_VERSION"
+          else
+            transformers_version="$DEFAULT_TRANSFORMERS_VERSION"
+          fi
+
+          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = 'workflow_dispatch' ] && [ -n "$MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_REF" ]; then
+            transformers_ref="$MANUAL_TRANSFORMERS_REF"
+          else
+            transformers_ref="$DEFAULT_TRANSFORMERS_REF"
+          fi
+
+          if [ "$transformers_source" = 'git' ] && [ -z "$transformers_ref" ]; then
+            transformers_ref='main'
+          fi
+
+          case "$selected_preset" in
+            '2.10.0-cpu')
+              torch_install_version='2.10.0'
+              torchvision_install_version='0.25.0'
+              torch_test_version='2.10'
+              ;;
+            '2.14.0-cpu')
+              torch_install_version='2.14.0'
+              torchvision_install_version='0.29.0'
+              torch_test_version='2.14'
+              ;;
+            *)
+              echo "Unsupported torch_preset: $selected_preset" >&2
+              exit 1
+              ;;
+          esac
+
+          {
+            echo "SELECTED_TORCH_PRESET=$selected_preset"
+            echo "TORCH_INSTALL_VERSION=$torch_install_version"
+            echo "TORCHVISION_INSTALL_VERSION=$torchvision_install_version"
+            echo "TORCH_TEST_VERSION=$torch_test_version"
+            echo "PYTORCH_INDEX_URL=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
+            echo "TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE=$transformers_source"
+            echo "TRANSFORMERS_VERSION=$transformers_version"
+            echo "TRANSFORMERS_REF=$transformers_ref"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+
+          echo "Selected PyTorch preset: $selected_preset"
+          echo "Resolved install tuple: torch==$torch_install_version torchvision==$torchvision_install_version"
+          echo "Resolved test expectation: torch=$torch_test_version"
+          echo "Resolved Transformers source: $transformers_source"
+
+      - name: Install PyTorch
+        run: |
+          pip install \
+            torch=="$TORCH_INSTALL_VERSION" \
+            torchvision=="$TORCHVISION_INSTALL_VERSION" \
+            --index-url "$PYTORCH_INDEX_URL"
+          python -c "import torch; print('torch:', torch.__version__, torch)"
+
+      - name: Install Transformers
+        run: |
+          case "$TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE" in
+            'pypi')
+              pip install "transformers==$TRANSFORMERS_VERSION"
+              echo "TRANSFORMERS_RESOLVED_REF=N/A" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+              ;;
+            'git')
+              git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/huggingface/transformers /tmp/transformers
+              cd /tmp/transformers
+              git checkout "$TRANSFORMERS_REF"
+              resolved_ref="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+              echo "TRANSFORMERS_RESOLVED_REF=$resolved_ref" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+              echo "Resolved Transformers git ref: $resolved_ref"
+              pip install .
+              ;;
+            *)
+              echo "Unsupported TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE: $TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE" >&2
+              exit 1
+              ;;
+          esac
+          python -c "import transformers; print('transformers:', transformers.__version__, transformers)"
+
+      - name: Install deepspeed
+        run: |
+          pip install .[dev,autotuning]
+          ds_report
+
+      - name: Reinstall selected Transformers
+        run: |
+          case "$TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE" in
+            'pypi')
+              pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall "transformers==$TRANSFORMERS_VERSION"
+              ;;
+            'git')
+              cd /tmp/transformers
+              pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall .
+              ;;
+            *)
+              echo "Unsupported TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE: $TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE" >&2
+              exit 1
+              ;;
+          esac
+          installed_version="$(python -c 'import transformers; print(transformers.__version__)')"
+          if [ "$TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE" = 'git' ]; then
+            requested_version='N/A'
+            requested_ref="$TRANSFORMERS_REF"
+            resolved_ref="$TRANSFORMERS_RESOLVED_REF"
+          else
+            requested_version="$TRANSFORMERS_VERSION"
+            requested_ref='N/A'
+            resolved_ref='N/A'
+          fi
+          {
+            echo "### Transformers provenance"
+            echo ""
+            echo "- Source: \`$TRANSFORMERS_SOURCE\`"
+            echo "- Requested PyPI version: \`$requested_version\`"
+            echo "- Requested git ref: \`$requested_ref\`"
+            echo "- Resolved git SHA: \`$resolved_ref\`"
+            echo "- Imported version: \`$installed_version\`"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+
+      - name: Python environment
+        run: |
+          pip list
+
+      - name: Pre-build JIT ops
+        # Rank workers JIT-load ops concurrently on first use; torch's build
+        # lock has no stale handling, so a leftover baton from a killed build
+        # wedges every later load. Build the hot ops once up front so tests
+        # only hit the disk cache.
+        run: |
+          python -c "
+          from deepspeed.comm.torch import build_shm_op
+          build_shm_op()
+          import torch
+          from deepspeed.ops.adam import DeepSpeedCPUAdam
+          DeepSpeedCPUAdam([torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(8))])
+          "
+
+      - name: Pre-download HF test fixtures
+        # Concurrent xdist workers downloading the same model race on the
+        # transformers cache lock and fail with PermissionError; populate the
+        # shared cache once so tests only hit it read-only.
+        run: |
+          HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 HF_HOME=/tmp/hf_home hf download bert-base-uncased
+
+      - name: Multi-rank tests
+        # Each phase keeps its own budget so a timeout reports as a timeout instead of
+        # swallowing the failures the other phase found; the exit code is classified in
+        # the next step rather than failing here.
+        run: |
+          unset TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST # only jit compile for current arch
+          cd tests
+          parallel_exit=0
+          sequential_exit=0
+          HF_HOME=/tmp/hf_home timeout 120m pytest $PYTEST_OPTS --maxfail=100000 --forked -n 4 unit/ --ignore=unit/v1 --torch_ver="$TORCH_TEST_VERSION" || parallel_exit=$?
+          HF_HOME=/tmp/hf_home timeout 25m pytest $PYTEST_OPTS --maxfail=100000 --forked -m 'sequential' unit/ --torch_ver="$TORCH_TEST_VERSION" || sequential_exit=$?
+          # A timeout (124) outranks the other phase's failures: the budget ran
+          # out, so more failures may remain undiscovered. Without this, the
+          # outcome depended on which phase happened to run last.
+          overall=$sequential_exit
+          if [ "$parallel_exit" -ne 0 ]; then
+            overall=$parallel_exit
+          fi
+          if [ "$parallel_exit" -eq 124 ] || [ "$sequential_exit" -eq 124 ]; then
+            overall=124
+          fi

+"""Classify the multi-rank CPU run's exit code for cpu-multi-triage.yml.

+the job log. The sentinel lives in this file instead of inline in the
+workflow's ``run:`` script because GitHub Actions echoes the whole script text
+into the log before executing it, and the classifier's ``head -1`` would pick
+up the echoed literal -- routing every failure as a timeout -- instead of the
+runtime line.

+
+import sys
+
+TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE = 124  # GNU timeout's exit code when COMMAND times out
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    raw = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "none"
+    if raw == "none":
+        # The test step never ran (setup/install died earlier); triage reports
+        # this as an unclassified failure, so emit no sentinel.
+        print("the test step never ran", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1

+    code = int(raw)
+    if code == 0:
+        print("multi-rank suite passed")
+        return 0
+
+    if code == TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE:
+        print("DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS=timeout")
+        return 1
+
+    print("DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS=test")
+    return code
+

+    raise SystemExit(main())

+    # would route the nightly to regression triage instead of the timeout path.

+    assert "DS_CI_FAILURE_CLASS=test" not in stdout
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+# DeepSpeed Team
+"""Contract tests for the DS_MULTIRANK_ONLY collection selector in tests/conftest.py.
+
+Each test builds a sandbox containing the real conftest.py and pytest.ini plus
+representative test classes, runs pytest --collect-only with the gate off and
+on, and asserts on which items survive collection -- the same observable
+surface the nightly multi-rank workflow relies on.
+"""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+TESTS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+SANDBOX_TESTS = '''
+import pytest
+
+
+class DistBase:
+    is_dist_test = True
+
+
+class PlainBase:
+    pass
+
+
+class TestClassWorldSizeTwo(DistBase):
+    world_size = 2
+
+    def test_class_level_multi(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class TestClassWorldSizeOne(DistBase):
+    world_size = 1
+
+    def test_class_level_single(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class TestNoWorldSize(DistBase):
+    def test_no_world_size(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class TestMarkRaisesToMulti(DistBase):
+    world_size = 1
+
+    @pytest.mark.world_size(2)
+    def test_mark_raises(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class TestMarkLowersToSingle(DistBase):
+    world_size = 2
+
+    @pytest.mark.world_size(1)
+    def test_mark_lowers(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class TestListWorldSize(DistBase):
+    world_size = [1, 2]
+
+    def test_list_has_multi(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class TestListAllSingle(DistBase):
+    world_size = [1, 1]
+
+    def test_list_all_single(self):
+        pass
+
+
+def test_plain_function():
+    pass
+'''
+
+
+def _collect(multirank_only: bool) -> list:
+    """Collect the sandbox suite with the gate off/on and return the node ids."""
+    root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="multirank_select_")
+    try:
+        for name in ("conftest.py", "pytest.ini"):
+            shutil.copy(TESTS_DIR / name, Path(root) / name)
+        (Path(root) / "test_sandbox.py").write_text(SANDBOX_TESTS)
+        env = dict(os.environ, DS_MULTIRANK_ONLY="1" if multirank_only else "0")
+        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", "test_sandbox.py"],
+                                cwd=root,
+                                env=env,
+                                capture_output=True,
+                                text=True,
+                                check=False)
+        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
+        # The conftest under test forces verbose mode, so --collect-only emits a
+        # tree of <Class>/<Function> lines instead of plain node ids.
+        ids = []
+        current_class = None
+        class_indent = None
+        for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
+            stripped = line.strip()
+            indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
+            if stripped.startswith("<Class "):
+                current_class = stripped[len("<Class "):-len(">")]
+                class_indent = indent
+            elif stripped.startswith("<Function "):
+                function = stripped[len("<Function "):-len(">")]
+                # A function at the class's own indentation level is
+                # module-level, not a member of the class above it.
+                if current_class is not None and indent > class_indent:
+                    ids.append(f"test_sandbox.py::{current_class}::{function}")
+                else:
+                    current_class = None
+                    ids.append(f"test_sandbox.py::{function}")
+        return sorted(ids)
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+ALL_ITEMS = [
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestClassWorldSizeTwo::test_class_level_multi",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestClassWorldSizeOne::test_class_level_single",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestNoWorldSize::test_no_world_size",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestMarkRaisesToMulti::test_mark_raises",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestMarkLowersToSingle::test_mark_lowers",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestListWorldSize::test_list_has_multi",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestListAllSingle::test_list_all_single",
+    "test_sandbox.py::test_plain_function",
+]
+
+MULTIRANK_ITEMS = [
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestClassWorldSizeTwo::test_class_level_multi",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestMarkRaisesToMulti::test_mark_raises",
+    "test_sandbox.py::TestListWorldSize::test_list_has_multi",
+]
+
+
+def test_gate_off_collects_everything():
+    # Catches an inverted or over-eager gate: local and regular CI runs must
+    # never lose tests to the nightly-only selector.
+    assert _collect(multirank_only=False) == sorted(ALL_ITEMS)
+
+
+def test_gate_on_keeps_only_multirank_items():
+    # Catches both directions: single-rank items leaking into the nightly
+    # (wasted budget, already covered by cpu-torch-latest) and multi-rank
+    # items being dropped (a silently green, test-free nightly).
+    assert _collect(multirank_only=True) == sorted(MULTIRANK_ITEMS)
+
+
+def test_mark_overrides_class_world_size():
+    # The selector must honor the same precedence as the launcher: a method
+    # mark beats the class attribute in both directions.
+    collected = _collect(multirank_only=True)
+    assert "test_sandbox.py::TestMarkLowersToSingle::test_mark_lowers" not in collected
+    assert "test_sandbox.py::TestMarkRaisesToMulti::test_mark_raises" in collected

+      # transformers_source=pypi. Scheduled nightlies and default manual runs
+      # install Transformers from Git and ignore this value.
+      transformers_version:
+        description: Hugging Face Transformers PyPI package version to install
+        required: false
+        default: '4.51.3'
+        type: string
+      transformers_source:
+        description: Hugging Face Transformers source for manual runs
+        required: false
+        default: 'git'
+        type: choice
+        options:
+          - 'pypi'
+          - 'git'
+      transformers_ref:
+        description: Hugging Face Transformers git ref to install when source is git
+        required: false
+        default: 'main'
+        type: string
+  schedule:
+    # Off the 00:00 cluster (cpu-torch-latest, formatting, amd-mi200, hpu) and away
+    # from modal-torch-latest at 10:00, so the two CPU suites never share a runner pool.
+    - cron: "0 4 * * *"
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
